stem: Northwind Components Ltd forecasts 2027 EBIT of USD 191 million, D&A of 46, capex of 59 and an increase in net working capital of 10.5 (all USD millions). The tax rate is 25%. Unlevered free cash flow (FCFF) for 2027 is closest to:

rationale.B: Incorrect. 140.75 adds the working capital increase instead of subtracting it.
rationale.C: Correct. NOPAT of 143.25 plus D&A, less capex and the NWC increase, gives 119.75.
rationale.D: Incorrect. 27.75 subtracts D&A instead of adding it back.

stem: For 2028 Northwind forecasts EBITDA of USD 256 million, D&A of 48, capex of 62 and an increase in net working capital of 10 (USD millions). The tax rate is 25%. FCFF for 2028 is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 120.00 taxes EBITDA (256 × 0.75 = 192) and forgets that D&A is tax deductible.
rationale.B: Correct. Tax is applied to EBIT, then D&A is added back and capex and the NWC increase are deducted.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 168.00 taxes EBITDA and then adds D&A back again, double counting it.

stem: A company reports net income of USD 112.0 million and interest expense of 25.0. D&A is 44, capex is 56 and net working capital rises by 10.5 (USD millions). The tax rate is 25% and there are no non-operating items. FCFF is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 129.25 adds the NWC increase instead of subtracting it.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 89.50 forgets to add back interest, leaving a levered (equity) cash flow.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 114.50 adds back the full 25.0 of interest; the tax saving on interest is already in net income.
rationale.D: Correct. Only after-tax interest of 18.75 is added back.

stem: An analyst building FCFF deducts interest expense before applying the tax rate, arguing that interest is a real cash cost. What is the main problem with this approach in a DCF that discounts at WACC?
options: It double counts the effect of debt financing, because the interest tax shield is already captured in the after-tax cost of debt in WACC
There is no problem; FCFF should always reflect all cash costs including interest
It overstates FCFF, because interest should be added back twice
It only matters if the company has negative net income
explanation: FCFF is cash flow before financing. The cost and tax benefit of debt enter through WACC; deducting interest in the cash flow as well counts financing twice.

rationale.A: Correct. Financing effects belong in the discount rate, not in unlevered cash flow.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Interest belongs in levered (equity) cash flow, which is discounted at the cost of equity, not WACC.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Deducting interest understates FCFF; nothing is added back twice.
rationale.D: Incorrect. The inconsistency exists whatever the level of profit.
